column3: 1.  Does sovereignty confer on states authority over cyber infrastructure located in their respective territories and over the actions they take with respect to that infrastructure?
column4: 2. Does sovereignty encompass the right to protect cyber infrastructure and safeguard cyber activity that is located in, or takes place on, its territory?
column5: 2(a) Does sovereignty encompass the right of a state to control government data and/or that of its nationals stored or transmitted inside their territory?
column6: 2(b) Does sovereignty encompass the right of a State to control government data stored or transmitted outside its territory?
column7: 2(c) Does sovereignty encompass the right of a State to control data of its nationals stored or transmitted inside its territory?
column8: 2(d) Does sovereignty encompass the right of a State to control government data stored or transmitted outside its territory?
column9: 2(e) Does sovereignty encompass the right of a State to control data of its nationals stored or transmitted outside its territory?
column10: 2(f) Is the exercise of such sovereign authority subject to international human rights law and other fundamental freedoms?
column11: 3. Is sovereignty a stand-alone, primary rule of international law, the breach of which can incur international responsibility?
column12: 3(a) Can violations of sovereignty not amounting to prohibited interventions constitute internationally wrongful acts?
column13: 4. Does the State indicate how to identify a violation of any stand-alone sovereignty rule?
column14: 5. Is it a violation of territorial sovereignty for an organ of a State, or others whose conduct is attributable to the State,
column15: 6. Can state cyber operations that cause physical effects in another state’s territory constitute a violation of sovereignty as a rule?
column16: 6(a) Do any physical effects constitute a violation?
column17: 6(b) Must the effects involve physical damage to computer infrastructure or other tangible things, or injury to persons, to constitute a violation of sovereignty as a rule?
column18: 6(b)(i) Must the effect of a cyber operation to computer infrastructure require repair or replacement of physical components to qualify as damage?
column19: 6(c) Do only cyber operations generating significant physical effects within another State’s territory constitute a violation?
column20: 7 Can state cyber operations that cause a loss to computer functionality in another State’s territory constitute a violation of sovereignty as a rule?
column21: 7(a) Is the rule violated by a cyber operation generating any functionality losses within another state’s territory?
column22: 7(b) Is the rule violated by a cyber operation generating significant functionality losses within another state’s territory?
column23: 7(c) Is the rule violated by a cyber operation generating systemic functionality losses within another state’s territory?
column24: 8. Can state cyber operations that interfere with another state’s “inherent governmental functions” constitute a violation of sovereignty as a rule?
column25: 9. Must there be proximate causation between the state cyber operation and the effects or interference prohibited by sovereignty as a rule?
column26: 9(a) Must the state cyber operation generate prohibited effects directly?
column27: 9(b) Do prohibited effects indirectly generated by a state cyber operation constitute a violation of sovereignty as a rule?
column28: 10. Can state cyber operations that deny access to or degrade data in the control of another State constitute a violation of sovereignty as a rule?
column29: 10(a) Do state sponsored ransomware operations violate the sovereignty of another State?
column30: 10(b) Can state cyber operations against data residing in cloud servers outside of a State’s territorial jurisdiction constitute a violation of sovereignty as a rule?
column31: 10(c) Does the exercise of one State’s law enforcement tools via cyber means in the networks or systems of another State’s territory violate the sovereignty of the latter State?
column32: 11. Do State cyber operations that interfere at any level with critical infrastructure in another State constitute a violation of sovereignty as a rule?
column33: 12. Can State cyber operations that cause significant national economic impacts for another State constitute a violation of sovereignty as a rule?
column34: 13. Does cyber espionage by one State in or transiting networks or hardware resident in another State constitute a violation of sovereignty as a rule?
column35: 14. Are violations of sovereignty assessed on a case-by-case basis?
